newsitem.title: UK: Tomkins plans share buy-back - UK papers.
newsitem.headline: Tomkins plans share buy-back - UK papers.

text.p: British newspapers reported on Sunday that industrial conglomerate Tomkins Plc would stage a policy U-turn this week and announce a share buy-back.
Chief executive Greg Hutchings had said in January that the engineering-to-baking group was not planning a share buy-back as it preferred to look for acquisitions.
But the Sunday Times said Hutchings was now likely to announce his intention of buying back up to five percent of the group's shares on Monday.
The Sunday Telegraph said the step was being considered "in an effort to boost (Tomkins') languishing share price".
Tomkins' shares closed at 263-1/2 pence on Friday compared with a high for the year of 297-1/2.
The Sunday Telegraph said Hutchings was not expected to announce any firm plans for a buyback.
"He is more likely just to raise the issue as a possibility and say it has not been ruled out," the paper said.
However, it added that this U-turn would be enough to stun the markets and help underpin the company's share price.
The company had no immediate comment. Tomkins is due to issue final results on Monday.
